pairs.difference: A: the oil lamp stands upright, dead-centre and symmetrical. It is a thin vertical shape that fills only the middle third of the width (box_width 0.43), with wide even green margins (0.115, at the top of the real range). B: the flashlight runs on a strong diagonal, and its yellow beam runs off the left edge. It spans 0.8 of the width and reads at a glance like the tilted water bottle on the real sheet.
pairs.fix: Make the oil lamp bigger and tilt it slightly. Let the glass chimney and brass base reach close to the top and bottom edges, and shift it a little off-centre so it fills most of the card.

pairs.difference: A: a small police car sits in the middle of a wide street scene, with houses, trees and sky around it. The car is short (box_height 0.48) and its margins (0.098) are wider than any real card's. At thumbnail size the houses and road compete with it. B: the red bike on the car's rack fills the card and is cut off by the right and bottom edges (margin 0). This matches the tight, cropped framing of the real lighthouse.
pairs.fix: Zoom in on the police car until it fills most of the card, with the bumper and roof light nearly touching the edges. Drop the houses and trees to a soft blurred hint behind it.

pairs.difference: A: the vending machine fills the card top to bottom in a 3/4 view, with tight side margins. B: the tape roll sits small in the middle of an empty green gradient, with a long cast shadow. Its margins (0.11) are just past the real maximum. The roll reads like a studio product shot, with a lot of empty space above it.
pairs.fix: Make the tape roll larger and turn it at an angle toward the viewer. Let it fill about 80% of the card, with the loose strip of tape reaching toward the lower corner, and shrink the empty green area above it.

pairs.difference: A: the open badge wallet is a flat, low strip across the middle of a dark wood table (box_height 0.47, below the real range). Most of the card is empty dark planks, and at thumbnail size the badge is a small yellow dot. B: the travel guidebook fills the card on a diagonal and nearly touches the edges. It is bigger than the real cards (0.53) but reads at once.
pairs.fix: Lift the camera closer so the open wallet with its gold badge fills most of the card, tilted at a diagonal. Push the badge large and toward the viewer, and keep only a thin band of wood around it.

pairs.difference: A: the bloodhound is wide and low and fills the card edge to edge, with its tail near the left edge. B: the two boxing gloves are wide and low, cropped tight at the right, with a horizon line at mid-height. Both sit at the wide, short end of the real range (box_width 0.9 and 0.95), and neither framing departs from the real cards in a way I can point to.

A: the magnifying glass sits on a large city map that fills the whole card. The map's pale lines and green park compete with the glass, so the hero itself covers only 0.2 of the card, below the real range. B: the green binoculars fill the card on a diagonal against plain wood stripes, and the lenses are read first.
pairs.fix: Make the magnifying glass the main thing and much bigger, filling most of the card on a diagonal. Show only a small corner of the map behind it, soft and low-contrast.

pairs.difference: A: the sailing ship fills the card. Its masts reach near the top, and the waves are cut off by the bottom edge, like the real lighthouse. B: the spyglass floats small on a diagonal in the middle of a striped cyan field. It is short (box_height 0.45), has wide margins (0.116), and covers 0.17 of the card, below the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the spyglass much larger and closer, with the big lens end near the top-left corner and the eyepiece near the bottom-right. Let it fill the card diagonally, with only a thin margin.

pairs.difference: A: the tilted vintage camera with flash sits centred on blue rings. Its margins (0.121) are slightly wider than real, but it reads at once. B: the orange music player sits upper-centre, with an earphone cable looping down. The earbuds pull a little attention, but the size (0.22) is within the real range. Neither one clearly breaks the real framing.

A: a single fedora sits centred on a purple gradient. It is wide and low but forms one clear shape. B: a pair of sneakers sits on a floor-and-wall set, and the flat horizon line cuts the card at mid-height. Two shoes side by side split the first read, and the orange wall above leaves the top third empty.
pairs.fix: Show one big sneaker in 3/4 view, filling most of the card, or two shoes overlapping closely. Use a plain radial background with no floor line, and leave no empty band at the top.

pairs.difference: A: the flower wreath is a small ring in the middle of a full doorway, framed by ivy and the doorframe. The wreath covers only 0.08 of the card, with very wide margins (0.28). The blue door and green leaves dominate, so at thumbnail size the door is read first. B: the brass doorknob is a large near close-up, with the door and room cut off by the edges, and the knob is read at once.
pairs.fix: Zoom in on the flower wreath so it fills most of the card, with only a strip of blue door showing around it. Remove the ivy border and the full doorframe.

pairs.difference: A: the red raised planter is shown as a whole scene, with a picket fence, bushes, sky, paving, and a watering can and trowel on its shelf. Many parts compete, and the hero is split into a frame shape. B: the sunscreen bottle stands large and centred, with sunglasses lying across its base. Two objects, but one clear focal stack against a simple green background.
pairs.fix: Show the raised planter box large and close, filling the card, with the herbs spilling over the top. Replace the fence and paving with a simple soft background, and leave out the watering can and trowel.

pairs.difference: A: the zip bag with a gold ring fills the card wide on dark wood, and the ring sits centred as the focal point. B: the tennis racket and ball cover only 0.19 of the card, below the real range. The racket sits diagonally on a flat green court, and a bright white court line crosses the whole card, competing with the racket.
pairs.fix: Make the tennis racket much bigger, running corner to corner so it fills most of the card, with the ball overlapping the strings near the front. Remove the court line or make it faint.

pattern: Generated cards place the hero small, whole, centred and in a neat frontal or symmetric pose inside a wide even margin (often over 0.1). They also tend to add scene context around it (island, map, street, fence, court line, ivy) that competes for the first read. Real cards push one hero big, often tilted and cropped by an edge, and keep the background simple.
